newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia coal exports hit by cyclone.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia coal exports hit by cyclone.

text.p: Australian coal exports to Asia, Europe and South America are being disrupted by cyclone Justin, which threatens Australia's northeast state of Queensland, officials said on Tuesday.
Queensland's three main bulk coal ports, one at Gladstone and two at Hay Point, were closed Sunday as seas rose.
Queensland is Australia's main high-quality coal producing state, while coal is Australia's largest export with 1995/96 exports valued at A$7.8 billion.
The coal is used in steelmaking and power stations around the world, but mainly in Japan, South Korea and Taiwan.

Coal was still being transported to the ports by train but could not be safely loaded because of heavy seas, Ian Dymock, spokesman for BHP Australia Coal, a unit of Australia's biggest coal producer the Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd,, told Reuters.
On Tuesday morning, three ships were queued at Gladstone while two were at Hay Point.
"Its not a huge line-up at the moment but if it goes on for a few days it will affect it," Dymock said.
With Australia the world's biggest exporter of coal, coal is shipped through Gladstone and Hay Point to 100 customers in 25 countries from the Queensland ports.

Hay Point ships about 25 million tonnes a year while Gladstone ships about 15 million tonnes a year. A second bulk coal port adjacent to Hay Point, at Dalrymple Bay, has a throughput of about 26 million tonnes of coal a year.
The annual total of 66 million tonnes of hard coking coal shipped through the ports translates to a weekly total of about 1.25 million tonnes.
Cyclone Justin, which is generating wind gusts of of up to 170 km an hour at its centre, remains 620 km (385 miles) east of the city of Cairns.
Australian meteorologists say the cyclone is expected to intensify today and that its main effect so far has been through tides of up to a metre (three feet) above normal, big seas and strong winds.
Hay Point is used by Central Queensland Coal Associates, a consortium of BHP, Japan's Mitsubishi Development Pty Ltd, the Australian Mutual Provident Society and QCT Resources Ltd.
A range of other Queensland coal producers ship through Dalrymple Bay.
These include RTZ Plc Co Ltd-CRA Ltd with Blair Athol thermal coal, MIM Holdings Ltd, Capricorn Coal Management Pty Ltd with German Creek coal and BHP with Goonyella coal.
There were no indications at this stage when the coal ports would re-open, Dymock said.
